description: DamageScanner is a Python toolkit from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam researchers for estimating direct losses from natural hazards. It overlays a hazard-intensity raster or grid with exposed land use or assets and applies a one-dimensional vulnerability curve to calculate damage. Flood depth was its original application, but the package allows another hazard when a suitable intensity-damage curve exists. Outputs are spatial and aggregate monetary-loss estimates for the input area and event. Resolution and period follow the supplied exposure and hazard layers, not a built-in global dataset. Source is free under MIT terms through GitHub and PyPI, with documentation and a software DOI. The README says the package remains in development, so reproducibility needs a pinned version and locally checked vulnerability functions. These are modelled losses, not observed repair costs. DamageScanner supports flood, storm and climate-risk simulations. The catalogue's model-global-river-flood-risk-framework-winsemius-2013 is a separate flood-risk method for comparison. The first review mentioned DamageScanner within a Jakarta case but did not prepare a separate tool record. No loss calculation was run.
